title: Listen, Learn & Live The Art of Enduring in The Truth

sense.text:
“And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” The man spoken of here is Adam. It is not talking about all people.

A lot of the time people think the image and likeness is only about looking like God. Man was formed of the dust of the ground, and we know God is black, Christ is black, the apostles were black, because the real Jews are black. The Caucasian race, which the Bible calls Esau, is cursed. But the image and likeness goes further than that: his image is righteousness and true holiness, and his likeness is beheld in righteousness. Man after God's image was meant to be righteous.

“And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.” The Lord gave Adam dominion over everything.

That is how we know it is not talking about everybody. It is Adam and the line coming from him, which would eventually be the twelve tribes of Israel.

precepts.why:
“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” Read together with Genesis 1:26, this shows what man was made from: the dust of the ground.

When God said “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”, he was going to his spirit to create man in his image and likeness, and that spirit is the commandments of God. The breath breathed into man is wisdom, given to us so that we should know better.

So the image is not only the hue of the skin. Man formed from the dust shares the elements of the ground, but the likeness of God is in the spirit God breathed into him.

“And that ye put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.” That is what it means to be made after the image of God: created in righteousness and true holiness.

When God said “Let us make man in our image”, he was making a man to be righteous and holy, not only a man who looks like him.

“As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.” Here is the likeness: it is in righteousness. Man after his image was meant to be righteous.

It is more than the hue of your skin. Being after his image means black and righteous, because black and wicked ain't the way to go: you're still the devil. A lot of times we say the white man's a devil, but there are black devils too. Just because you are black don't make you special unless you are righteous. It's the laws of God that make us special.

Solomon says, “I myself also am a mortal man, like to all, and the offspring of him that was first made of the earth”. He that was first made of the earth is Adam, formed of the dust of the ground in Genesis 2. Solomon is the offspring of that man, of the line that came from Adam.

sense.text:
“God hath granted me to speak as I would, and to conceive as is meet for the things that are given me: because it is he that leadeth unto wisdom, and directeth the wise.” God is the one who leads us to wisdom, and the wise are directed by him.

If you have enough wisdom to know that God is directing you, he will direct you away from evil. He will show you how to avoid it.

“For in his hand are both we and our words; all wisdom also, and knowledge of workmanship. For he hath given me certain knowledge of the things that are, namely, to know how the world was made, and the operation of the elements”. God gave Solomon to understand how this world was made and how the elements operate.

The operation of the elements is what we call the periodic table today. The elements in soil are the same ones in man: oxygen (46% of the soil, 65% of a human), iron, calcium, sodium, potassium, magnesium. When God made us from the dust of the ground, he took from all these elements and gave them different percentages to make man. That is the formula he showed Solomon. What we call God's creation, or his miracles, is that he understands how to work these elements to form man, to form land, to form sea.

This is what Esau is trying to do with his so-called science. He is Frankenstein, trying to become God and do what God has done.

Wisdom is “Kind to man, stedfast, sure, free from care, having all power, overseeing all things, and going through all understanding, pure, and most subtil, spirits.” If those are the attributes of wisdom, I want to be tethered to her, so that I can discern and understand why people do the things they do.

A man who will not own up to his error wants others to share it. That is gaslighting: he tries to make you feel guilty, tugging on your heart to make you feel a way for something he is in error about. Being subtle to speech, you understand what he is doing. The one in error is supposed to wear down the footsteps; he wants you to chase him, and that's not how this goes.

“For wisdom is more moving than any motion: she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness.” Wisdom is pure. There is no defiled thing in wisdom, and she moves through everything you can conceive.

Look outside at a tree that takes in carbon dioxide and gives us back oxygen: that is the wisdom that created it. God's wisdom is in everything we do, see and touch, seen and unseen. It is wisdom and her pureness operating.

“For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty”. Wisdom, which is she, is the breath and the power of God. The power of God is the word of God, which is wisdom; they are all synonymous.

That is the breath that was breathed into us in Genesis 2. It was wisdom, that we should know better. He gave it to us.

And the pure influence is the commandments of the Lord, which are pure and enlighten the eyes.

precepts.why:
“For the word of God is quick, and powerful”. This is the power of God, which is the word of God, which is wisdom. They all mean the same thing. The word of God is this book, and the word of God is Christ. It is one pureness, one avenue, with no variableness in what it means.

That is why the Christian church has destroyed the minds of a people, making them believe you can separate Christ from the commandments. It makes no sense: he is the word. You can't believe on Christ and not keep the commandments, and you can't keep the commandments and not believe on Christ. That's an oxymoron. But the witchcraft called Christianity has separated them so far that it has even been said that if you keep the commandments you're sinning. Whoever thought of that sermon was reaching that day, and somebody sat there saying Amen. Your church makes you dumb as hell.

The word of God is “sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” The word of God will cut you, and it lets you know the intents of the heart. When a man comes with a pity party you have seen a thousand times before, wisdom tells you he ain't for real; it's game.

“Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.” He is directly tethered to wisdom. So if you are tethered to Christ, you are tethered to wisdom, and then you know BS when you hear it. You know the intention of a person's heart when they speak: that is false speech.

Sometimes you tell a man, stop talking, I'm trying to help you, because in the multitude of words there is sin. There's a lot of explaining for a little situation, and he keeps digging a deeper ditch, thinking he is making sense, not realizing he's embarrassing himself. A spiritual man discerneth all things. We could be wrong, we're not 100% with everything, we're learning ourselves; but if you are tethered to wisdom, you understand the intents of people when they speak, and you understand false speeches.

“The belly devoureth all meats, yet is one meat better than another.” Why is one meat better than another? Because you can taste it and say, I like this one better than that one. You have a palate.

“As the palate tasteth divers kinds of venison: so doth an heart of understanding false speeches.” The same way you can taste meat, a heart of understanding discerns false speech. You listen to somebody and you know, this is BS, this ain't adding up.

It happened at Passover: listening to a brother, after a while it started to sound like murmuring, and Captain Sham was called to hear what was being said. That brother would have been better off just keeping quiet. That is the discerning heart of a man tethered to wisdom, which goes through all understanding.

sense.text: “There is no speech nor language, where their voice is not heard.” A class might come out in English and you might speak Spanish, but don't worry: we'll translate it for you, we'll get to your language, even your sign language. If it is for you, you are going to get that verse.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” The law is perfect, making wise the simple.

Converting doesn't just happen, like you close your eyes and wake up different. It comes through trial, error and correction. That is the converting, and you are supposed to be happy about it.

“The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” The commandments of the Lord are pure, the pure influence that flows from the glory of the Almighty. They enlighten your spiritual eye to see things clearly, to understand false speech, to understand when you are going in the wrong direction. They are supposed to light your path, and the statutes are supposed to rejoice your heart.
“The fear of the Lord is clean, enduring for ever: the judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether.” It is clean, it is pure, it endures forever, and it is righteous and true.

“More to be desired are they than gold, yea, than much fine gold: sweeter also than honey and the honeycomb.” It is sweeter than honey. But then it gets bitter, because now you start to learn about yourself. It's all right, though, because the law of God converts the soul. It's only a problem when your soul ain't getting converted.

When you come to this truth, prepare your soul for temptations, trials and tribulation. People come in with rose-colored glasses, thinking everything is going to be perfect. No: it starts unmasking who you are, who I am, what we have to fix to get right. It's sweet until you start dealing with who you really are.

“Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.” There is a reward for keeping the laws of God. The Lord does not ask us to keep the laws with nothing in return; he is a just and fair God. We have to decide if we want to be converted.

“Who can understand his errors? cleanse thou me from secret faults.” Cleanse me from the things that people don't know I am dealing with.

Sometimes a class comes out and it is talking right about you, and you say, does he know? That is the Lord: you said you wanted wisdom, and he gives to every man liberally, but now he is going to show you. You need to be cleansed; we need to be cleansed.

“Keep back thy servant also from presumptuous sins”. If you want to be kept back, God has to send the word to you. Keep me back from presumptuous sins, deliver me from my secret faults: this is a prayer we ask of God. Then he sends the prophets to tell you, so why are you upset? You asked God to cleanse you; he has to show you what needs to be cleansed.

So the first key is listening. There is an art to listening, and the greatest gift a young person can have is to just listen. You will save yourself so much headache. Be neutral to hear what is being said, then examine yourself whether it is true or not, and if it is, fix it. Stop lying to yourself.

“Let them not have dominion over me”: don't let my sins have dominion or rulership over me; I need to be delivered from them. “Then shall I be upright, and I shall be innocent from the great transgression”.

“Let the words of my mouth, and the meditation of my heart, be acceptable in thy sight, O Lord, my strength, and my redeemer.” You are asking the Lord to let your words and your meditation be acceptable. If you want your words and your thoughts to be acceptable, you have to open this book, read what the will of God is and learn it. And when the word comes to you, you have to accept it for what it says.

precepts.why:
Correction is how the soul is converted, and you are supposed to be happy when it comes: “Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil”. The person telling you what you are doing wrong is doing you a kindness, and it is a blessing.

“Which shall not break my head”: it ain't going to kill you. Somebody telling you that you are doing evil is supposed to kill the old man in you, but it is not going to kill you physically. People don't want to hear that; they don't want to know the errors of their ways. “For yet my prayer also shall be in their calamities.”

“All iniquity is as a twoedged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed.” We just read that the word of God is a twoedged sword, and the word of God cures. So why can't these wounds be healed?

“He that hateth to be reproved is in the way of sinners: but he that feareth the Lord will repent from his heart.” That is why: you hate to be reproved. You hate to be corrected, and that's why you can't get right. The word of God does cut, but you can be healed if you accept what it is saying. That means somebody is telling you, and you are listening.

When the word comes to you, you have to accept it, for “the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow”. Quick means alive. This word is alive; it's not like a textbook.

The word of God is going to affect you deeply, to the deepest part of your thought process. It's going to cut. You feel sick to your stomach, like you're going to throw up, an emptiness like hunger. You sit in class with the word coming out and you can't even lift your head, because you know he's talking to you. That's good, because if you don't feel that, you're a reprobate.

“Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath”. Do more listening than talking, because if you're talking you can't hear what's being said. And after you hear what's being said, why are you angry?

You said, God, show me the errors of my ways, cleanse me. So he sends the prophets to tell you, and now you're mad at them for telling you. You don't want to be right; you want to continue your way and expect God to love you. It doesn't work like that. You might as well go back to church on Sunday.

That's why the people killed the prophets: they kept coming to tell them what they were doing wrong, and they didn't want to hear it, to the point that they killed them just to shut them up. Let's not be those people.

sense.text:
“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” The letter is to the twelve tribes that were scattered abroad, the ones that were living as sinners, serving gods of wood and stone. Living that way, we were spotted.

So count it joy when God starts showing you who you are. To live an unspotted life in this world, we have to learn what we were doing wrong so we can fix it. So why are you mad? That is the whole purpose.

“My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.” Why count it joy to fall into temptations? Because you are learning about yourself, your faults, what you have to fix. Being tried also shows you are a son of God, and the Lord sees you fit to be chastised so that you come out of the trial increased.

Some people come to this truth and never knew they deal with a spirit of unforgiveness. They can't let somebody off the hook for something that happened ten years ago, five years ago; they still harbor it. Some leave a brother in purgatory, reminding him of something he did years ago that he hasn't done again. The scripture says all manner of sin is forgiven; you have to allow him to grow up out of it, not hold him captive to his past action. That is something you are battling, and the word of God will show you what you have to fix. That is a trying of your faith.

Let patience have her perfect work: you have to work through it, that you may be perfect and entire, meaning whole, wanting nothing, lacking nothing. You don't want to lack any type of wisdom. When you fall into temptations, it is to build you up.

“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally”. How do we ask of God? Do you think it just floats down from heaven? No: you have to study, you have to open a book. But how do you know unless you have a teacher? Somebody has to teach you, even if you are watching a video. When he teaches you, you grow in understanding.

And as you grow, you realize, I had not known sin. Paul was an expert in the law, and he had not known lust except the law said, Thou shalt not covet. It revealed it to him, and now he knew he had to fix that in himself.

So you pray, you ask of God, and then you go to a house of learning and learn. And when you are uncertain about counsel you have heard, you go to God, and God will direct your path.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” You ask in faith for God to show you about you so you can fix you, knowing that God will direct you on the right path. Then the scripture comes to you correcting you, and now you're wavering. When you waver, you are trying to dodge correction.

Something tossed around is forever moving. It's not straight, it's not steady, it doesn't go head on.

“A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.” With God there is no variableness, but with man there is: double-minded, jumping all over the place, can't take it, making excuses, always responding, always got something to say, never listening. You tell him once, twice, maybe three times, and after that you have to stop talking, because the words of God are not affecting him. There is no magic scripture that can compel him. It's a character flaw in some people, and it's what holds them back.

You criticize a man constructively, and before you can get the sentence out he is already answering you. He's not listening to understand; he's listening to respond. A man of wisdom hears from a neutral position and takes in all the information. Then he discerns whether it fits him or not, and if he's still uncertain, he goes to God.

“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him.” How do you know what you can endure unless you go through it? How do you know you can bench 315 until you put 315 on the rack and see if you can push it? Then you realize you can't push it yet, so you exercise some more. You're asking for muscles; well, you got to lift, you got to go to the gym, and we're going to put weight on there.

“Let no man say when he is tempted, I am tempted of God: for God cannot be tempted with evil, neither tempteth he any man”. Don't blame God. Lord, it ain't me, you put that big thick big booty woman in front of me. God says, stop, bro. I put a 9 millimeter in front of you, a knife in your hand, a crackpipe in the room; I didn't pull the trigger, I didn't stab you, I didn't smoke it. So why are you blaming me?

God doesn't tempt any man. When you're tempted, you are supposed to resist.

“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” That's you, bro. So maybe you need to keep quiet, stop talking and listen. Don't get mad with God. God is just showing you what your vice is. If she ain't your vice, you ain't going to get caught. Now you've found out what your vice is, and that's what you're fighting.

To be enticed is when something appeals to you and you give in to it. You are drawn away, but then you entertain it. That's on you; that's your choice. You're supposed to turn away.

“Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.” Every good gift comes down from God, and here is a good gift: wisdom. If you lack it, God will give it to you.

With God there is no variableness. He is not tossed to and fro; he is not double-minded; it's straight. There is a constancy with God and his wisdom. It is pure, undefiled. You don't have to add to it, take away from it or change it; it is always going to be constant. But with man there is variableness.

“Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” Of God's own will he begat us with the word of truth. We were formed in his image, in his likeness, to be righteous.

The literal firstfruits given to God had to be perfect. When you brought an animal, it could not be spotted. So we are to keep ourselves unspotted.

“Let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath”: this is how we get unspotted. God sends teachers to show us how to get right, and we get cleansed, we get fixed, because we are swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.

“Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness”. Superfluity of naughtiness is excess of naughtiness, of sin. He is talking to the twelve tribes that were scattered, who were in all manner of idolatry, and they have to lay that aside. You weren't tempted of God; you were tempted of your own lust. You came asking, and now you're being shown, so why are you talking, why aren't you listening, why are you mad?

“And receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.” The word is engrafted in the heart. Receive it with meekness, humility, humbled down. The word is able to save your soul if you receive it, and if you would keep quiet and listen, you'll be able to receive it.

“But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.” You can't just hear it; you have to do it. That's the only way it works: you have to apply the word that you've heard. And if you heard it, somebody had to be speaking for you to hear it.

You deceive yourself if you ain't going to do what you heard. You're lying to yourself, going through the motions like you're in the truth. You're not in the truth.

The battle begins right here. When you start to hear it, you reason within yourself, and when your mind will not accept what you heard, right is coming in but wrong is there. That's a war.

“For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.” That glass is the Bible. You look at yourself when you read the book: wow, this is me, I have to fix it. But the forgetful hearer sees himself and forgets what manner of man God was trying to show him he was.

You look in a mirror and see a big booger in your nose. You don't like how it looks, so you turn your head away. You can't see it no more, but is it still there? You can turn your head, but the booger ain't going nowhere. You can close this book and you're still a sinner; close it and you're still a thief. You don't want to see yourself, because when you see yourself you see how evil we really are, and people don't want to deal with that.

So leave if you want. Nobody's going to be here holding your hand. You got a better plan; let's see how it works out for you. But if you go, you are drawn away of your own lust.

“But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.” He is not a forgetful hearer of what he was taught. He applies what he was taught, and he gets a blessing.

“If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.” A man may seem convicted in what he believes: I believe this Bible, the real Jews are black, Christ is black, we're going to get the kingdom. But he doesn't know when to shut up, and he deceives his own heart with excuse after excuse.

His religion is vain; it ain't going to get him nothing. You can put on the shirt, put on the fringes, grow a beard, stop eating pork, but if you're not willing to deal with what you've got going on in your head and be honest about it, you're wasting your time. You might as well go back to the world.

“Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.” We all fall short, so to be unspotted we have to learn what we were doing wrong. The world is all messed up, and we have to be unspotted.

Now that we're unspotted, what are we supposed to do? Teach. We had a guide that directed us in the right way; without that guide we wouldn't have it. The affliction of the fatherless and widows goes back to the temptations. What are they lacking? A guide. They don't have a hedge, they don't have a father, they don't have anybody to lead them. Now that you're unspotted because you learned about yourself, it's time to go out and help people in the same thing so they can become unspotted.

But how are you going to teach them if they're not swift to hear and slow to speak? How can you help them if they get mad and dodge every time you tell them something?

precepts.why:
Unforgiveness is a trying of your faith. “Sufficient to such a man is this punishment, which was inflicted of many.” He got punished for his action because he was in error. “So that contrariwise ye ought rather to forgive him, and comfort him”: on the contrary side, now that he paid his punishment, you ought to forgive him and comfort him.

Some brothers don't have the spirit to comfort. They look at comfort as weak. But the Bible says forgive and comfort him, “lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with overmuch sorrow.” If you don't allow him or her to grow out of the situation, they feel it's hopeless, there's no chance for repentance, they can never get right, and you destroy a brother.

“Wherefore I beseech you that ye would confirm your love toward him.” It is not a weak nature to forgive a brother and confirm your love: I see you fighting, you're trying to get right, we're here for you. You don't have to baby him, but don't hold him on something he has moved on from. It could destroy him.

“For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye be obedient in all things.” He served his punishment and accepted it; now let's see if you can move forward. Can you forgive? Paul was not there with them, but if they forgave, he forgave also, “Lest Satan should get an advantage of us: for we are not ignorant of his devices.” One of Satan's devices is being unforgiving.

There are things you may not forget: a brother stole, and you may not let him in your house again. That's not what this is about. It's when he ain't stealing again and you keep saying, remember that time you stole, you thieving ass, that was five years ago. Yeah, that nigga's a thief. That's something you're battling within you. You are unforgiving, and Satan's got you.

This is asking of God for wisdom: “When I was yet young, or ever I went abroad, I desired wisdom openly in my prayer. I prayed for her before the temple, and will seek her out even to the end.” He prayed openly for wisdom and sought her even to the end, because wisdom will direct your path.

“For thou savedst me from destruction, and deliveredst me from the evil time: therefore will I give thanks, and praise thee”. I will thank you, because you deliver me from that evil path.

“I directed my soul unto her, and I found her in pureness”, the same pureness read of in Wisdom of Solomon 7. I redirected what I was doing and directed my soul to wisdom, because wisdom in her pureness will direct my path and save me, and with wisdom I will avoid the punishment. That's what we're all here for: I want to get myself right, to be a better servant, a better husband, a better father, for God to use me. So teach me, God. But somebody has to teach you.

“My heart was troubled in seeking her”. As he sought her, he started realizing all the issues he had, and the severity of what God is talking about: eternal damnation. At first it sounds good, putting on fringes, keeping the feast days. Then you learn, damn, I'm a hateful ass brother, I'm a murmurer, a backbiter, I can't get past porn, I can't get past lying. Your heart is troubled.

“Draw near unto me, ye unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.” Somebody is going to teach you, to teach you how to draw nigh and how to direct yourself. And now they're teaching you and you're mad? Do we understand what we signed up for? You said you wanted wisdom; here it is. If you're mad, you don't really want wisdom. You want church.

So you pray, you ask of God, and then you go to a house of learning and learn. “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts”: know what I think, how I process your information. Try me means measure me against your word.

“And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.” Tell me, Lord, if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the right way. That is what we all are asking God to do. If any man lack wisdom, he asks of God, and he is asking God to show him his errors. So you count it joy when you fall, because you asked, show me all my wicked ways, that I can fix them.

The wavering man is trying to dodge correction. “Be not ashamed to confess thy sins; and force not the course of the river.” Here's the river; it's flowing. You don't want the river to go that way, so you try to reroute it. Forcing the course of the river is trying to dodge correction and make it seem like it is something that it is not.

“But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.” That's a river. Let judgment run down. Let it run. Don't waver and try to get around it; don't try to force the course and divert it. Let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.

“I will bear the indignation of the Lord, because I have sinned against him”. He is taking accountability: I will bear the indignation, the judgment of God, because I have sinned. “Until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me”.

Don't try to get around the cause, don't deviate from the judgment, don't make excuses. Stop wavering. You asked God to show you; he has shown you where you're wrong, and now you're trying to bypass it: maybe I'd be better if you brothers called me and checked in on me; it's your fault. Do you think this is Disney and this is a ride? Nobody's joining you on that pony ride.

“He will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.” He brings me forth to the light because I don't dodge what I asked for. God, show me my secret faults, my errors; I want to get better. Now that he is showing me, it ain't the time to start dodging; it is time to accept what it is. We all fall short.

That is how you endure the truth: listen, learn and live. There's no special recipe. When it comes, take your medicine like a big boy and move on like a big girl. It's not the infraction that shows who a person is; it's what they do afterwards. If that were the test, none of us would make it, because all of us are wrong. Do they take their medicine, the scriptures? Some have big talk, and as soon as correction comes they ghost and make excuses, because of pride and ego.

When people come into this faith they pray for wisdom and discernment, but the carnal man does not see things spiritually, and they will not listen to the men appointed before them. “Thus saith the Lord, I brought this people out of bondage, and I gave them my commandments by my servants the prophets”. The prophets were given the commandments to teach the people.

“Whom they would not hear, but despised my counsels.” It wasn't only the counsel of the prophets they despised. The prophets opened up the scriptures and showed them, thus saith the Lord, to help them overcome what they were dealing with, and that was the counsel God truly gave. It came by men, but God inspired that counsel.

Whoever brings correction your way, it's for your benefit, and they are inspired by the Lord to direct you in the path you should walk. So discern and humble yourself. Be quiet and listen to what they're telling you out of the scriptures; they are showing your error. Be humble, learn, listen. That is how we grow. The carnal man or carnal woman will cause you to resist the direction in which God wants you to go.

All scripture is given by inspiration of God and is profitable for proof, for instruction in righteousness. This book is not to tote your ego and make you feel good because everybody thinks they're righteous. If the Lord showed us who we are, we would be ashamed. If it wasn't for the mercy of Christ and the promise he made, none of us would be here. He wants us to change, and to change we have to identify what we were doing wrong. For that, somebody has to tell us.

If you are uncertain, you go to God, and he will direct your path. “But be continually with a godly man, whom thou knowest to keep the commandments of the Lord”. Always be around godly men: not men that appear godly, but those you know are keeping the laws of God. How would you know? If you are tethered to wisdom, you will have a discerning spirit.

“Whose mind is according to thy mind”: your mind is a godly mind too. Can two walk together unless they be agreed? If your mind is not godly, if you have secret faults you aren't fixing, there's a good chance you're not around a godly man. And if you are around a godly man, he is going to tell you about yourself, and you shouldn't be getting mad.

“And will sorrow with thee, if thou shalt miscarry.” If you fall into error, he will sorrow with you and fight with you to help you. That's why we have to see the fight in you. A hand will always be reached out, once, maybe twice; but if there's no fight in you, he washes his hands, and his conscience is clear.

“And let the counsel of thine own heart stand: for there is no man more faithful unto thee than it.” Nobody is more faithful to you than your own mind. But if you're not a godly man, your thought process is broken, corrupted, and your decisions won't be made right. So when a godly man gives you counsel, listen from a neutral place and really receive it, rather than listening with your mind already made up. Why come asking if you already know what you want to do?

“For a man’s mind is sometime wont to tell him more than seven watchmen, that sit above in an high tower.” Watchmen in a high tower look down and get a broad view. You see your life from ground level, straight across, and there are things in your life a counsellor can't fully see. He may say, don't move, trust God; you may say, I can't pay my rent, I'll be evicted next month. Brothers give counsel sometimes and are overbearing. His counsel might be good counsel, but you have to at least be neutral to hear what's being said.

“And above all this pray to the most High, that he will direct thy way in truth.” You listen to the counsel, you process it, then you go to God, and God will direct your way in truth. If you are a godly man, you have wisdom, and God directs the wise: don't leave, everything will work out, or go ahead, this will work out for you. “Let reason go before every enterprize, and counsel before every action.” Seek counsel from a godly man you know keeps the commandments, then go to God and ask him to direct your path.
To the twelve tribes scattered abroad: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. God scattered Israel and made our remembrance cease.

Scattered, we were going to serve gods of “wood and stone.” When we were serving gods of wood and stone, we were spotted. So when James writes to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, it is to the ones that were living as sinners, and they have to learn what they were doing wrong to live unspotted.

When you're tempted, you resist. “Submit yourselves therefore to God.” Take the counsel; submit yourself to God. “Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.” How do you resist him? The beginning of verse 7: you submit yourself to God, and then you resist the devil.

“Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you.” How are you going to draw nigh to God? Somebody's going to teach you and you're going to learn. You go to the house of learning to draw nigh. That's what you are doing now. And God will draw nigh to you; he will give you a way to escape.

“Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.” That's what was read in James 1:8. Now that you hear the correction about how to get right with God, you've got excuses. You see the sin and the error in front of you, because somebody is reading it to you, and you turn away from it.

Hearing but not accepting is a battle, a war. “From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members?” That's where the fight comes from. Something is at war inside of you because you're being told something, and something in you is adverse to correction; you don't want to accept it.

Captains who have sat in counsel know it. You tell a man what he's doing wrong: you don't listen. And he repeats it back, so what are you saying, I don't listen? Then his eyes squint like he's confused. You just said it; why are you repeating it? After 31 years of this, it's comical sometimes. It ain't his sight that went bad. It's the battle in his mind at that moment, clashing, and it manifests in his face.

“For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” The word of God is pure; there is no variableness to it, and there should be no confusion in what's being said. If you were really unsure, you would say, what did I lie about? Show me the lie; help me understand. Instead you're confused. That's the war happening inside: right is coming in and you're warring with it because you don't want to accept it.

Then you wonder why good things are withheld from you, why you can't move forward. You're a liar, a thief, a murderer, an adulterer; it is being identified to you and you cannot reason with yourself. You have strife in your heart.

“This wisdom descendeth not from above, but is earthly, sensual, devilish.” It's devilish, and it is deceiving you, as James 1 said: deceiving your own selves.

When a brother starts to correct them, people don't like it: they pull away, hold a grudge, and start speaking evil of him. But “Speak not evil one of another, brethren.” What are you supposed to do? “Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord”.

“Therefore to him that knoweth to do good, and doeth it not, to him it is sin.” You know what's being said is right, but you don't want to do it because you're struggling. Your sin is what you are struggling with; that's where the war is, because you don't want to accept the prophet telling you.

That's all of our people in the streets right now. Tell them what they're doing wrong and they're ready to kill you, ready to fight you for teaching the Bible. You hate to hear it because it convicts you. It lets you know your life is in shambles, and you're evil, and you're the devil.

Part of deceiving yourself is justifying yourself. “If I justify myself, mine own mouth shall condemn me”. You condemn yourself. In Psalms 19 the word of God that comes from the teachers is supposed to cleanse you. To justify yourself is to clear yourself: you deceive yourself into thinking, I'm already cleansed, I'm already clear, I don't need the reproof and the instruction the teachers bring.

Sometimes you have to let people suffer. They ignore warnings and repeat patterns, and some only change after life corrects them. It is good to be afflicted, so that you may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing. Officers, brothers, teachers and instructors can't carry everybody.

sense.text:
“But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.” This is back to the face in a glass of James 1. This book is the glass of the glory of the Lord, and we behold it with an open face.

An open face is a face set unto the Lord God, seeking him by prayer and supplication, going to the book and confessing that we have sinned. When we really behold his face openly, we will change, into the same image from glory to glory. There is supposed to be a change in us when we accept, we pray, and we understand that we have sinned against God.

precepts.why:
The open face explained: “And I set my face unto the Lord God, to seek by prayer and supplications, with fasting, and sackcloth, and ashes”. With an open face I set my face to God and go to him by prayer and supplication.

“In the first year of his reign I Daniel understood by books the number of the years, whereof the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, that he would accomplish seventy years in the desolations of Jerusalem.” Daniel understood it by the writings of the prophet Jeremiah. He was seeking God openly, and he went to the book.

Then he “made my confession, and said, O Lord, the great and dreadful God, keeping the covenant and mercy to them that love him, and to them that keep his commandments; We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly”. And: “Neither have we hearkened unto thy servants the prophets, which spake in thy name to our kings, our princes, and our fathers, and to all the people of the land.” We would not listen to the prophets you sent to show us what we were doing wrong. That is beholding with an open face: confessing, and owning that we would not listen.

sense.text: “Therefore seeing we have this ministry, as we have received mercy, we faint not”. Now that we have this ministry, we don't faint.

“But have renounced the hidden things of dishonesty, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.” This is what we are supposed to do when we seek him openly, face to face: renounce the hidden things of dishonesty, meaning the secret sins. Not walking in craftiness: not talking too much, trying to find a way to snake around it.

Blessed is the man whose conscience does not condemn him, because he has examined himself against this book: I've renounced the things I was doing, and I no longer do them.

“But if our gospel be hid, it is hid to them that are lost”. The gospel we teach is to be beheld with an open face, renouncing sin. If you don't understand that you have to renounce sin, you're lost.

That's the Christian church: we're no longer under the laws of God, we're under grace, you can't call me a sinner, I've been saved. You have not renounced the hidden things of dishonesty. You're an undercover homo, still fornicating, still smoking weed, effeminate, popping gum with your sister's lip gloss on, singing soprano. You have not renounced it. You're lost.

Those who are still in sin, who will not renounce being dishonest and keep living as sinners, are the lost. If you think you found God, you're lost, and your religion is vain. It's a level of insanity to ask God to deal with you and then not want to do what God says.

precepts.why: The hidden things of dishonesty: “Surely he knoweth your inventions, and what ye think in your hearts, even them that sin, and would hide their sin.” You can't openly seek his face while you're hiding your sins, trying to get around them and not deal with them.

“I brought you up with gladness; but with sorrow and heaviness have I lost you: for ye have sinned before the Lord your God, and done that thing that is evil before him.” The gospel is hid to them that are lost, and here are the lost: those that have sinned and done that thing that is evil before him, still in sin, not renouncing the hidden things of dishonesty.

sense.text: “The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God; As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee. The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.” God said, I'm going to send my messenger before me, which was John, and he is going to teach you, to get you right, to prepare for me. That is the job of the prophet, the apostle, the teacher: to show you.

“Now as he walked by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers. And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.” After John, Christ is bringing these men in. They are coming to get right.

He “saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets. And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, and went after him.” Do you think when he was walking with them he wasn't showing them all their errors?

precepts.why:
Christ had to expose to Peter what was in him. “Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.” I prayed that your faith won't fail, and when you are converted, go and strengthen your brethren. When you get right, then go teach the people. He is showing him that he still has things to work on: you want to walk with me, I'm going to show you what your problems are.

“Lord, I am ready to go with thee, both into prison, and to death.” And Christ answers, “I tell thee, Peter, the cock shall not crow this day, before that thou shalt thrice deny that thou knowest me.” Didn't you just hear what I said? Stop talking, Peter: you're going to deny me three times. You ain't there yet; your mind ain't right yet.

Peter afterwards was the head of the church, but there were things he had to reconcile within himself, and he had to get right. If Christ could tell him that, he can tell us. God opens his book and shows us; we behold ourselves in it, and what we see is there for us to fix. He sends prophets to show you how to get right, and the worst thing is to deny it. It doesn't feel good going through it, and sometimes medicine hurts, but if you're sincere you'll take your medicine, move on and get better. If you don't, you'll be an example of what not to do.

sense.text:
“Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me”. God told the prophets to go and show the people their sinful deeds. That is the theme: listen.

Those who give instruction cannot use the scriptures just to bash brothers, to weaponize the scriptures, correcting everybody else while not correcting their own lives. You'll be the brother that is wise and teacheth many, yet is unprofitable to himself. Some hold brothers to a higher accountability than they are willing to hold themselves, expecting perfection while they have hidden sins. Don't walk in hypocrisy. Sometimes your skirt has to be pulled up to show your shame, and even that is God loving you, because he could leave you there and let you find out after death.

precepts.why:
“And go, get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.” Whether they hear or forbear, our job is to go and tell them.

Then “the spirit took me up, and I heard behind me a voice of a great rushing”, and the noise of the wings of the living creatures: these are the angels.

“Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.”

As a prophet and a teacher, it is required of us to tell you what you're doing wrong, because if we don't, that blood is on our hands. It's not that we even have a choice. If you call yourself a prophet or a teacher, your job is to correct the people and help the brother.

If you see a brother in error and you don't correct him, what are you? “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.” We have no choice but to tell them what they're doing wrong, or we hate our brother in our heart.

sense.text:
“I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.” God said, I'm going to return to my place. They have to seek me, but they have to get afflicted first. That's how our people are: we have to be afflicted as a people.

Our people don't understand right now, and the afflictions are just starting. We've been getting killed in the streets by police, but that is only the prelude to what is about to happen. Esau is turning back the civil rights era right now. Memphis, maybe the blackest city in America, has been gerrymandered and carved up and parceled out so that no black man can win a congressional seat there, and it's happening in Texas and everywhere. And we need that, because black people swear they're going to vote their way out of this crap. We need to be afflicted, to see the devil for who he is, and he is consistently showing himself.

As we see these afflictions happening, we have to get our minds right, because we know the fierce anger of the Lord is coming, and we want to be on the right side with God. So, Lord, show me where I'm in error so I can fix it, so that when your decree brings forth I'm lined up on the right side. It's our job to warn our people and bring them to repentance, and when they come, to help them reform their ways. But they have to be willing to listen, and many will have to be judged first. In America we are so comfortable; hard to us is cancelling Netflix and buying one Starbucks a week.

precepts.why:
“All Israel in like manner cried most earnestly unto the Lord, because their death was before their eyes.” That is when they're going to come. When death is before their eyes, they'll cry earnestly and start looking for God, and that's where they're going to learn. When they come, we're going to show them what they're doing wrong and how to get right.

They arrested a congressman lawfully in the house; the state troopers kicked him out, and he cursed them, I'm an elected official. Yeah, but you're leaving. The white guilt is out the window.

Right now our people are still confused about who the devil is. The Christian church is full of crap. Those over fifty remember when the church was where black people met and planned; now, where do you hear the churches talking about the civil rights laws being turned back? Our people are being hung in 2026, their organs cut out, and it's called suicide, and the black church says nothing; we're the only ones talking about it. Black church, you all full of crap; y'all better repent, because y'all evil as hell. You ain't really about changing your people; you want to sing and dance people to sleep. All them pastors are weak men. If you ain't teaching our people that they are Israelites, that they must repent and keep God's commandments and believe on Christ the black Messiah, you ain't on the front line of nothing. Don't go to church; stay on the street before you go to church.

“Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired; Before the decree bring forth, before the day pass as the chaff, before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you, before the day of the Lord’s anger come upon you.” That's what we have to do: gather together before the decree brings forth, before our people cry earnestly with death before their eyes.

“Seek ye the Lord, all ye meek of the earth, which have wrought his judgment; seek righteousness, seek meekness: it may be ye shall be hid in the day of the Lord’s anger.” Seek the Lord: ask and you shall receive, and he gives to every man liberally. Seek righteousness, seek judgment, you meek: that means you don't have it yet. You're walking in error, so now you're seeking it.

When you come to the house of learning, somebody is showing you your error. Don't get mad and leave, because leaving from here you go back out there to deal with the fierce anger of God. While you're here, you're going to learn how to turn away from your sins.

sense.text:
“If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.” People ask how we mobilize. The secret recipe is that we keep God's commandments, we enforce the laws of God, and we believe on Christ; you can't have one without the other.

Humble themselves: we just read that. Seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways, and he will hear us and heal us.

“Now mine eyes shall be open, and mine ears attent unto the prayer that is made in this place.” God does not hear the prayer of sinners; when we turn, his eyes and ears are open. “For now have I chosen and sanctified this house, that my name may be there for ever: and mine eyes and mine heart shall be there perpetually.” He will be with us forever if we turn back.

“And as for thee, if thou wilt walk before me, as David thy father walked”. Did David not sin? He did, but he repented, he changed, and he was called a friend of God. We have the same thing: you have to acknowledge and change. And after you change, you teach transgressors his ways, going to the fatherless and the widows to teach them.

“But if ye turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments, which I have set before you, and shall go and serve other gods, and worship them; Then will I pluck them up by the roots out of my land which I have given them”. To forsake is to abandon, desert, leave entirely, in a breach of duty or affection: you totally turn your back. That's a reprobate.

He will “make it to be a proverb and a byword among all nations.” That is the reason we are all in hell today: we got jammed up. He was speaking to Solomon.

precepts.why:
What was Solomon's problem, besides sinning? “Better is a poor and a wise child than an old and foolish king, who will no more be admonished.” He couldn't take correction. Nobody could tell him anything. He was an old foolish king who would no longer be admonished, and from that trickled all his other problems.

Even Solomon at the end understood the whole duty of man: to fear God and keep his commandments. But he shouldn't have had to go through that, because all wisdom was given to him and he saw his father's life. He wanted to experience the world, when we are supposed to be unspotted from the world. Some brothers here are the same: they can't be told, they get offended. When you keep repeating something to a man who doesn't want to hear it, he's a wash.
“Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way: and he that hateth reproof shall die.” The one who forsakes the way finds correction grievous, and he that hateth reproof shall die.

“He, that being often reproved hardeneth his neck, shall suddenly be destroyed, and that without remedy.” Often reproved means every time he is corrected he will not accept it, so you keep correcting him, and after a while his neck becomes hardened. He becomes stiff-necked. The scriptures have no effect; there's no contriteness, no shame. You see brothers stood up over and over, and they get hardened.

The word of God is supposed to move you to change. You can't be the same person you were ten years ago, still needing somebody to motivate you to go do the work. Something is disconnected. If you ain't changing, it's one of two things: you're a heathen or you're a reprobate. The word of God changes you and can cure you. If it isn't working, you may not be Israel, or you're a reprobate and the kingdom ain't for you; somebody has to be the two thirds.

sense.text: “And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” Why are you calling on me when you refuse to do the things I say? You're wasting your time.

“Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.” The man who heard and did is like one who dug a deep foundation. He was warned that a flood was coming, and he prepared himself.

So we need to prepare ourselves before the decree brings forth, before the fierce anger of the Lord, and be rooted in Christ: not just a hearer, but a doer. Had the flood come before he got right, his house would have been destroyed. He had to be exposed: you ain't right, get yourself right and prepare for what's coming. And he said, I heard you, and now I'm going to do it, as opposed to, I heard what you said, I heard what you said, and nothing changes. If you heard, there has to be some type of change. The house had to be shored up.

“But unto the wicked God saith, What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” This is twofold: it is talking about Esau, but in a smaller form it is you calling Lord, Lord and not wanting to do the things he says.
“Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” You hate to be instructed. I don't want to hear what you've got to say: you're hardened now.

“When thou sawest a thief, then thou consentedst with him, and hast been partaker with adulterers.” You love evil better than good, and you chose to be with it. You're supposed to resist the devil, not entertain him, and you're entertaining it. “Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit.” You're full of lies and deceit, walking dishonestly, handling the word of God deceitfully.

“Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” A brother admonishes you, and now you're angry behind it and speaking against him. Why are you mad? Why is it bothering you?

“These things hast thou done, and I kept silence; thou thoughtest that I was altogether such an one as thyself: but I will reprove thee, and set them in order before thine eyes.” Just because he didn't do anything right away, don't think you're going to get away with it.

“Now consider this, ye that forget God, lest I tear you in pieces, and there be none to deliver.” This is talking about Israel, because other nations can never know God. They can't forget God, because they don't have a God.

“Whoso offereth praise glorifieth me: and to him that ordereth his conversation aright will I shew the salvation of God.” That's how we know it's Israel, because the salvation is only to Israel.

precepts.why:
“Admonish a friend, it may be he hath not done it: and if he have done it, that he do it no more. Admonish thy friend, it may be he hath not said it: and if he have, that he speak it not again. Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, and believe not every tale.”

A brother is also a friend, and a friend admonishes. So when a brother admonishes you, he is doing what a friend does. Don't turn around and speak against him and slander him.

A friend and a brother are synonymous. “A man that hath friends must shew himself friendly: and there is a friend that sticketh closer than a brother.” Some friends are closer than a brother. So when Psalms 50 says you speak against thy brother and slander thine own mother's son, it is the friend who admonished you that you're slandering.

sense.text: “And God hath set some in the church, first apostles, secondarily prophets, thirdly teachers”. The Most High sets up apostles, teachers and leaders, and the whole point behind it is to build back his kingdom. These men are to guide you and show you a better way. That's their job: to show you how to serve God. That's the purpose they were sent for.
“But covet earnestly the best gifts: and yet shew I unto you a more excellent way.” They are there to show you a more excellent way.

precepts.why:
“And Samuel said unto the people, Fear not: ye have done all this wickedness: yet turn not aside from following the Lord, but serve the Lord with all your heart; And turn ye not aside: for then should ye go after vain things, which cannot profit nor deliver; for they are vain.”

“For the Lord will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake: because it hath pleased the Lord to make you his people.” It pleased God to make us his people. He's not going to forsake us, but you have to turn to him.

“Moreover as for me, God forbid that I should sin against the Lord in ceasing to pray for you: but I will teach you the good and the right way”. That's the point: I'm not going to stop praying for you, but my job is to teach you the good and the right way to walk. That's what God charges teachers with, and you have to be willing to listen.

“But if ye shall still do wickedly, ye shall be consumed, both ye and your king.” If you still do wickedly, you're going to die. But I'm going to do my job and teach you; what you do with it is on you, and my hands are going to be clean. We do our part, and the people on the receiving end have to accept it.

sense.text: “Lead me in thy truth, and teach me: for thou art the God of my salvation; on thee do I wait all the day.” Look what David is asking for: lead me in thy truth and teach me. Lead me, and teach me.

precepts.why:
Lead me and teach me: “Thus saith the Lord, thy Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel; I am the Lord thy God which teacheth thee to profit, which leadeth thee by the way that thou shouldest go.” He leads you in the direction you should go.

God has sent the prophets, and many have killed the prophets. That's why it says be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath, because people hate the word of God so much they want to kill us. We go out to teach and get guns pulled on us by Christian folk, while dudes drive by selling crack. Are we the enemies because we tell the people the truth? No. You're simple, and you don't want correction. Either repent, or die in your sins.
